This year I will still keep cotton as my main crop, because on 9.5 mu I cannot gamble too much. Cotton is slower to return money, but I know how to manage it, and with well water I can hold it steady. I will put about 4 mu into cotton, 3 mu into cauliflower, and 2.5 mu into stevia. That way I spread risk. If one crop sells poorly, I still have the others. I have farmed 35 years, so I do not start from zero. I look at what worked last year, then I adjust a little. Around here, if fertilizer looks short, yield drops first and it is hard to make back later, so I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than watch the field go weak.

For cotton, I will use a hybrid that people around me already planted well, not some strange new one. I will plough the land, put base fertilizer down first, and then chase topdressing in stages. Cotton needs steady feeding, especially nitrogen, but I will not let it grow all stalk and no boll, so I will keep phosphorus and potassium in too. With well irrigation, I will water about 4 times if the season is normal. On pests, I will not save money too hard on cotton, because once aphids, red spiders, or bollworms get ahead, I will spend more later. For cauliflower, I will use a hybrid too, because the heads are more uniform and easier to sell. This crop is greedy for water and fertilizer, so I will feed it heavier than cotton, especially nitrogen and potassium. I will irrigate more often and spray more often, because soft rot, caterpillars, and aphids come fast if I relax. For stevia, I will use an improved type that has been giving stable leaf yield nearby. I will manage it cleaner and finer, with more small irrigations, because once the stand is uneven, the harvest is troublesome. I will not push pesticide too high on stevia, but I will keep the field clean and protect the leaves. My whole way is simple: keep cotton steady, use cauliflower for cash flow, and keep stevia as an extra earner without letting input cost run wild.
